data: Which of the lines on the plot best represents the 'Zipf-Mandelbrot' distribution?

The question asks which line on the plot best represents the Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution. From the caption, we know that there are three lines in the plot: one for the Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution, one for the quadratic distribution, and one for the word rank data points. The Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution is represented by a green dashed line, while the quadratic distribution is represented by a blue dotted line. The word rank data points are represented by red crosses.

To determine which line best represents the Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution, we need to look at the shape of the line. The Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution is known to have a power-law decay, meaning that the frequency of words decreases as their rank increases, but with a slower rate than the Zipf's law. This means that the Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution will have a steeper slope than the quadratic distribution but a flatter slope than the word rank data points.

Looking at the plot, the green dashed line (Zipf-Mandelbrot) has a steeper slope than the blue dotted line (quadratic) but a flatter slope than the red crosses (word rank data points). Therefore, the green dashed line best represents the Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution.
